thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert: increased 5xx and token latency observed for inference clusters in eu-central-3a. Packet loss and TCP retransmits detected on host NICs. Auto-escalating to on-call. docs/retrieval: https://internal.redwood/infradoc/az-issues :rotating_light:
ana (oncall): seeing big spike in 5xx rate on /v1/generate from eu3 region, 4xx stable. Errors look like connection resets + 'write: broken pipe' from runtime. Prioritizing mitigation now.
mike (sre): confirmed. Host-level network errors across multiple nodes in eu-central-3a. CTL plane shows same healthchecks flapping. 10-15% pod loss for inference pools.
sophie (infra): also seeing delayed control-plane DNS responses for internal service discovery in eu-central-3a (avg rtt jumps 200ms -> 2s). Could be AZ networking tier degradation. Filing AWS ticket, contacting account team.
jess (support): we already have 3 customers reporting timeouts and degraded latency on production, some have started triggering retries from SDKs. Escalating to CS leads.
nana (oncall): action plan: 1) remove eu-central-3a endpoints from low-latency routing for hosted API (soft failover) 2) scale up eu-west-1 and eu-north-1 capacity to absorb traffic 3) enable cross-region fallback routing in gateway for customers with strict SLOs 4) roll canary traffic back once metrics stable. Starting step 1 now.
mike (sre): runbook note: to toggle routing policy run:
```bash
# invert weight for eu3a in routing config
redwoodctl route update --region eu-central-3 --weight 0.0
redwoodctl route update --region eu-west-1 --weight 0.6
redwoodctl route update --region eu-north-1 --weight 0.4
```
I pushed the first command, should take effect within 45s.
sophie (infra): pushing BGP/edge changes to reduce egress from the affected AZ. Also enabling additional NAT gateway paths for eu3 to reduce single-path congestion.
incident-bot: Change recorded: route update by mike (sre) at 1841234689.
jess (support): tagging impacted customers in crm: C-1002, C-4198, C-7321. Notifying them of temporary cross-region routing.
mike (sre): started emergency migration of reserved inference pools from eu3a to eu-west-1 (drain + recreate). Using live migration plan to avoid cold starts: pre-warm replicas with weights 0.3 before shifting traffic.
nana (oncall): monitoring KPIs: 5xx-> target <0.1% within 10m, p95 latency -> back to baseline. Creating a short incident timeline for postmortem.
cloud-eng-bot: AWS support case opened: case# 1234567890 - "ec2 eni packet loss and partial host network impairment in eu-central-3a". Account rep pinged.
sophie (infra): noticed some DNS TTLs were extended long (600s) and caching caused some clients to still hit eu3a until TTL expiry. Implementing proxy-level fast-fail for 502/504 to force re-resolve.
mike (sre): added temporary redirect rule at edge: if 5xx rate > 1% for a backend, failover immediately and mark backend unhealthy for 120s. This is aggressive but reduces customer impact.
jess (support): got confirmation from C-1002 that latency improved after 3m. Two other customers still seeing intermittent errors, probably due to SDK retry windows.
nana (oncall): handoff note for next oncall (overnight): mitigation in place, eu3a traffic weight at 0, eu-west-1 and eu-north-1 absorbing load. AWS investigating physical NIC saturation. Please continue to monitor cloud networking metrics and customer reports. If packet loss persists > 20m, escalate to infra lead and consider zone evacuation.
mike (sre): adding run: `redwoodctl pool prewarm --region eu-west-1 --model all --replicas 30` and `redwoodctl pool drain --region eu-central-3 --grace 120`
incident-bot: Incident P1 created at 1841234567, status: active, severity: P1, priority: customer-impacting.
jess (support): updated public status page: "We are experiencing degraded performance in eu-central-3 region. We are routing traffic to other regions and working with cloud provider."
ana (oncall): final check before handoff: dashboards look stable, 5xx rate down to 0.08%, p95 latency within 10% of baseline. Leaving notes in ops-runbook and creating postmortem stub. Handoff to night oncall @mike (sre) at 1841240300. Good job team :thumbsup:
